admission.justification: Two scoping rules were weighed with measured landing evidence; every later landing, publication and validation must obey the chosen population.

alternatives.option: Judge a row as new or edited only in a history file the route under judgment publishes: open files always, and at leaf publication files not closed in a base, reusing the validator's existing checked_history_files notion.
alternatives.reason: The architect's run-2 ruling 4 settles which files the rule judges; both rules now agree on what published by this route means.

alternatives.option: Judge every parsed history file, exempting only rows identical at the same path in a comparison base or frozen tree.
alternatives.reason: The sprint line holds none of the master's history files, so every landed unlabelled row counted as new: nine violations on the landed history, measured before the re-versioning.
alternatives.reconsider_when: History files become comparable across lines at landing time, so a landing base always holds the rows it judges.

consequences: Master and checkpoint landings pass over closed history files whichever leaves they belong to.
Leaf publications judge files not closed in a base whatever the hand-set flag says.
The writer's own validation judges open files only and is not a publication.
context: As first built, the rule judged every parsed history file, so the master's landing onto the sprint line refused with nine violations on landed frozen rows; D47 gave the architect the authority for the run-2 rulings that re-scoped it.
decider: Architect, run-2 ruling 4 under developer direction D47.
